name: A holy man's movement
about: A barefoot friar preaches to the hungry that the great are sinful; a lord embraces or hunts him, rivals cry heresy, and the friar becomes an order, an exile or a martyr.
title: The Preaching of {friar}

name: Brother {first}
Friar {first}
new.memory: The gods spoke to me in a ditch outside {lord.seat}. I have walked barefoot since.

goal.text: bring the great of {lord.house} to their knees before the gods

fade: The crowds thin as the harvest comes in. {friar} walks on to other villages, and {thread} is forgotten.

beats.speaker: friar
beats.text: A barefoot friar called {friar} comes to the villages around {lord.seat}, preaching that the great are sinful and the poor will inherit the land.

memory.lord: A friar called {friar} preaches in my villages that lords are sinners.

beats.speaker: friar
beats.text: Hundreds follow {friar} from field to field. The tithe barns of {lord.house} stand half empty; the people give to the friar instead.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {lord} kneels in the mud before {friar} and is blessed. The faithful of {lord.seat} take up pikes and march behind the friar's crowds.

memory.lord: I knelt in the mud to {friar} and was blessed.
memory.friar: {lord} of {lord.house} knelt to me. The gods are working.

beats.speaker: rival
beats.text: {rival} of {rival.house} writes to the King that {lord} harbours a heretic and arms a rabble against honest lords.

memory.lord: {rival} called me a heretic's dog before the King.
memory.rival: I warned the King about {lord} and the friar.

beats.speaker: friar
beats.text: No one dares come for {friar} while {lord}'s pikes stand round {friar.him}. The preaching goes on, and spreads.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {lord} sends riders to take {friar}. They find {friar.him} preaching on a hillside to a thousand people, and the riders do not dare.

memory.friar: {lord} sent riders to take me. The people stood in their way.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {friar} is hanged from the bridge at {lord.seat}. By morning the rope is gone, cut into relics.

memory.lord: I hanged {friar} from the bridge at {lord.seat}. The people took the rope for relics.

die.how: I was hanged from the bridge at {lord.seat} for speaking the truth.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: The hungry rise in {friar}'s name. They burn the tithe barns of {lord.house} and stone {lord}'s stewards in the road.

memory.lord: The poor rose in the hanged friar's name and burned my barns.

beats.text: The relics are sold and resold at fairs. In a few years the bridge at {lord.seat} is only a bridge.

beats.speaker: friar
beats.text: {friar} is taken in the night and put on a ship across the sea in chains. The preaching stops; the poor do not forget the face.

beats.speaker: friar
beats.text: {friar}'s followers build a house of prayer outside {lord.seat}, with {lord}'s stone and the poor's labour. They call themselves the Barefoot Brothers.
Nobody much comes to hear {friar}. {friar.He} walks on to other lands, preaching to the crows.
{friar} dies in a hovel outside {lord.seat}, and within a season the poor are praying to {friar.him}.

memory.lord: {friar} is dead, and the poor pray to {friar.him} now.

beats.speaker: friar
beats.text: {lord} dies, and {friar} preaches that it was the gods' judgment. The new lord of {lord.seat} listens carefully.
